metadata.title: Agent Proving Ground
metadata.purpose: Final-project pitch: an AI coding agent run in an isolated sandbox, traced, and checked by deterministic tests.
metadata.note: Narration copied verbatim from BEAT-PLAN.md, except B04 and B10 (revised by the author 2026-10-13) and B12 (added by the author 2026-10-13); B06 and B07 last sentences revised by the author 2026-10-13; B06 last and B07 first sentences moved to future tense by the author 2026-10-14. sentences.text: Hi, I'm Tushar.
Have you ever wondered, when an AI coding agent tells you it's done, whether it really is?
Today, the honest answer is often: check it yourself.
My final project will do that check for you.

beats.narration_text: This is Agent Proving Ground. It will run an AI coding agent on small tasks inside an isolated Kubernetes sandbox, record every step it takes, and check whether it actually did the task.

production_viz.mechanic: Three boxes in a row: Sandbox → Trace → Check

sentences.text: This is Agent Proving Ground.
It will run an AI coding agent on small tasks inside an isolated Kubernetes sandbox, record every step it takes, and check whether it actually did the task.

beats.narration_text: When it’s done, it will be a public GitHub repository: a Go harness, ten to twenty synthetic coding tasks with automatic checks, saved traces of every run, an evaluation log, and a failure analysis.

production_viz.mechanic: Sketch of a repo folder tree: harness/, tasks/, traces/, EVAL-LOG.md, FAILURES.md. Label: Constructed
production_viz.label: Constructed — not built yet.

sentences.text: When it’s done, it will be a public GitHub repository: a Go harness, ten to twenty synthetic coding tasks with automatic checks, saved traces of every run, an evaluation log, and a failure analysis.

beats.narration_text: An agent saying "done" is not the same as the task being done. One command will answer three questions. Did the change pass the checks? Did the agent stay inside its sandbox? Did my latest prompt change make things worse?

production_viz.mechanic: The word "done" in a speech bubble, then three check boxes appearing: checks passed · stayed in sandbox · no regression

sentences.text: An agent saying "done" is not the same as the task being done.
One command will answer three questions.
Did the change pass the checks?
Did the agent stay inside its sandbox?
Did my latest prompt change make things worse?

beats.narration_text: Before planning this, I looked at two existing tools. E2B is a service that runs AI-generated code in sandboxes. Langfuse is a tool that records LLM traces and scores them. Each covers one piece. Mine will join sandbox, trace, and check into one small loop you run on your own machine, where pass or fail comes from tests run inside the sandbox, not from another model’s opinion.

production_viz.mechanic: Two separate puzzle pieces: "Sandboxes — E2B" and "Traces & scores — Langfuse". They slide together into one piece: "Proving Ground"

Mine will join sandbox, trace, and check into one small loop you run on your own machine, where pass or fail comes from tests run inside the sandbox, not from another model’s opinion.

beats.narration_text: The reader is an engineer or hiring manager on an agent infrastructure team. In the first sixty seconds, they'll read the README, run one command, and see a table: each task, pass or fail, and why. Then they can open any trace and see exactly what the agent did.

beats.narration_text: It will show four skills from this course: a prompt contract for every task, an agent loop I write myself in Go with the Claude API, verification from deterministic checks, and evaluation I can repeat and compare across runs. It will be built for one laptop, not for production traffic.

beats.narration_text: The real risk is learning Go and Kubernetes at the same time, so the evaluation never gets built. So I’ll build the harness and checks on plain Docker first, then move them onto kind by a fixed date. If I miss it, I’ll ship the Docker version and log why.

So I’ll build the harness and checks on plain Docker first, then move them onto kind by a fixed date.

beats.narration_text: I picked this project because it mixes skills I have with skills I want. I've already built LLM evaluation and cloud infrastructure with Docker, Terraform, and AWS, in a public project you can check on GitHub. Go, Kubernetes, sandbox isolation, and trace design are new to me. I want to work on the infrastructure that AI agents run on, and building this is how I'll learn it.

New: Go · Kubernetes · sandbox isolation · trace design
